correctness.rationale: The N=1 and N=2 cases are exact. For N=3 the standard uniform P1 mass and stiffness matrices give an exact rational dimensionless generator, which is diagonalized by the discrete sine basis. Every semigroup entry is then explicit. Only the (1,3) and (3,1) entries can be negative, and their sign reduces to a strictly convex two-exponential function with exactly one positive zero. Exact arithmetic and high-precision replay confirm all matrix identities and bracket the root.

evidence: Thomée's 2015 full chapter proves that a normal triangulation with nondiagonal mass matrix cannot have a nonnegative standard Galerkin solution matrix for all small times and proves eventual positivity when H^{-1}>0.
The same chapter defines the positivity threshold and reports numerical thresholds for uniform triangulations of the two-dimensional unit square.
Jin--Lazarov--Thomée--Zhou extend the same framework to subdiffusion and again state small-time failure for nondiagonal mass and eventual positivity under H^{-1}>0.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These general results establish the phenomenon but do not determine the smallest one-dimensional uniform system, and their numerical examples do not analytically reduce the N=3 semigroup to one scalar sign channel.

originality.rationale: The broad consistent-mass positivity defect and eventual positivity are classical and explicitly treated as prior work. Required semantic-index searches and literature searches did not locate the minimal one-dimensional classification N<=2 versus N=3 or the exact three-node threshold equation. A full primary chapter was inspected through its definitions, small-time theorem, eventual-positivity theorem, and numerical-threshold section; its worked example is two-dimensional and tabulated numerically rather than the present one-dimensional closed form. Residual terminology risk remains.
residual_risks: The 2015 CMAM article could not be inspected end-to-end because its public PDF fetch timed out; only metadata and a searchable excerpt were available.
An older one-dimensional finite-element or positive-semigroup note may contain the same N=3 calculation without using the phrase positivity threshold.
No statement is made for N>=4, so the finding should not be read as an all-mesh threshold law.

value.rationale: The smallest mesh size at which a standard consistent-mass discretization first violates a PDE maximum-principle property is a natural structural boundary. The exact scale-free reappearance time gives a reproducible benchmark rather than another qualitative counterexample, and the N<=2 proof rules out smaller systems. This can directly test mass-lumping, limiter, and time-integration implementations.
